errors: Most of the 65 errors are understandable, and several are not model errors at all but **label errors** in the data set: the two most confident 'mistakes' are photos of corrugated cardboard labelled *paper*, which the model calls cardboard with 100% confidence, a round metal lid is labelled *glass*, and a crumpled brown paper bag is labelled *trash*. Other errors involve **items made of two materials** – glass bottles in a cardboard carrier, a yoghurt cup with a paper sleeve, a paper cup with a plastic lid – for which a single label is ambiguous, or **materials that imitate another one**: a gold-coated paper plate and shiny black plastic predicted as metal, metallised crisp packets and crumpled plastic film predicted as paper. A few are unusual images, such as a collage of food photos with text. Part of the remaining error is therefore a limit of the labels and of single-label classification for composite packaging rather than of the model.
gradcam: For the correctly classified images the heat-maps concentrate on the objects and on material-specific details rather than on the background: the body of the glass bottle, the opening and rim of the crushed can, the printed coupons of the paper flyer, the plastic bottle and the sandals. The two most confident 'mistakes' are two copies of the same photo of corrugated board labelled *paper* (a near-duplicate pair, kept together in the test set by the group split); the model looks precisely at the corrugated edge – the feature that identifies cardboard – which supports the view that these are label errors rather than model errors. The cardboard example, an old stained sheet from a stock-photo website, shows attention spread over a corner and the border, a reminder that some decisions rest on weaker cues. Overall the explanations give no sign that the model relies only on the white studio background. (A first version of this analysis hooked the network layer before its activation function, which produced inverted heat-maps; using the activated feature maps, as Grad-CAM requires, fixed it.)
gradcam_short: Grad-CAM shows that the model looks at the objects – the bottle, the can opening, the sandals – and not at the white background; for the corrugated board labelled 'paper' it focuses on the corrugated edge, so those 'errors' are really label errors.
